key_insight: PI-MFA reconstructs flow fields with B-splines while explicitly enforcing PDE physics, so the result is continuous, differentiable, and more physically consistent than purely data-driven interpolation.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a compact way to generate reliable surrogate flow fields for analysis, differentiation, and visualization even when the input data are coarse or physically inconsistent.
method: Tensor-product B-splines build a compact continuous field representation.
Spline control points are optimized to balance data fit with PDE residuals, initial conditions, and boundary conditions.
Exact analytical B-spline derivatives are used to evaluate physics constraints efficiently.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical tests on 1D convection-diffusion, 2D coupled Burgers, and 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes problems, where PI-MFA reduced PDE residuals and improved balance-law consistency versus standard/regularized MFA and was computationally competitive with physics-informed neural networks.
watch_item: Performance depends on having the right PDE constraints and optimization setup, so model misspecification or poorly chosen weighting between data and physics could limit reconstruction quality.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed B-Spline Framework for Continuous Approximation of Flow Data
